extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent owners, third-party requesters, and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how examiners should decide requests for ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302/303/304, prepare grant/denial decisions, handle prior art, timing, petition/review procedures, and patent owner statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question (SNQ) may be based on non-requested claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The finding of 'a substantial new question of patentability' can be based upon a claim of the patent other than the ones for which reexamination was requested (35 U.S.C. 303(a)). The Office may also initiate a reexamination on its own initiative of a non-requested claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the examiner will ordinarily concentrate on claims for which reexamination is requested, the examiner is not limited to those claims and can determine an SNQ as to other claims without necessarily finding an SNQ as to the requested claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision must discuss all requested claims and limit discussion in order to whether SNQ raised
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision on the request for reexamination should discuss all of the patent claims requested for reexamination. The examiner should limit the discussion of those claims in the order for reexamination as to whether a substantial new question of patentability has been raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2242 for discussion of claims subject to prior decision; amendments/new claims in copending proceedings are not considered when deciding a request (see MPEP § 2240 II.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art sources for SNQ determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination under 35 U.S.C. 303(a) whether a substantial new question of patentability is present can be based upon any prior art patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.515(a) and 35 U.S.C. 303(a) allow consideration 'with or without consideration of other patents or printed publications' beyond those relied on in the request. Examiner may also consider patents/printed publications of record from 37 CFR 1.501 submissions (if 1.98 compliant). If additional prior art can be readily obtained to supply deficiencies, examiner may perform a limited additional search where there is reasonable likelihood such art will supply a necessary deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination must be made on claims in effect at time of decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination should be made on the claims in effect at the time the decision is made (37 CFR 1.515(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision must identify claims/issues, references relied on, and provide rationale for each SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for reexamination is granted, the examiner's decision will conclude that a substantial new question of patentability has been raised by (A) identifying all claims and issues, (B) identifying the patents and/or printed publications relied on, and (C) providing a brief statement of the rationale supporting each new question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must identify at least one SNQ and explain how the prior art patents and/or printed publications raise such a question. The examiner should indicate, insofar as possible, his or her initial position on all issues identified in the request (without rejecting claims) so comment may be received in the patent owner's statement and the requester's reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific points to address for each SNQ (A–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: As to each substantial new question of patentability identified in the decision, the decision should point out: (A) the prior art patents and printed publications which add some new teaching as to at least one claim; (B) what that new teaching is; (C) the claims that the new teaching is directed to; (D) that the new teaching was not previously considered nor addressed in earlier concluded examination/review or final court holding of invalidity and was not raised in pending reexamination/supplemental examination; (E) that the new teaching is such that a reasonable examiner would consider it important in deciding to allow the claim being considered; and (F) where the question is raised, or where it is not clear that a patent or printed publication pre-dates the patent claims, a discussion as to why the patent or printed publication is deemed to be available against the patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2247.01 for an example of a decision granting a request for reexamination. In simple cases, examiner may adopt the requester's reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art listing and copy-supplying requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior art relied on should be listed on a form PTO-892 if not already listed on PTO/SB/08A/08B or PTO/SB/42 (or equivalent). A copy of a reference should be supplied only where it has not been previously supplied to the patent owner and requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper grounds not considered in SNQ determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments based on grounds not based on patents or printed publications (e.g., public use, sale, abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c)) are improper for reexamination and are not considered or commented upon (see 37 CFR 1.552(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such arguments are raised by a requester, the examiner should note that such grounds are improper for reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing, form paragraphs, and correspondence instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 22.01 should be used at the beginning of each decision letter and form paragraph 22.73 at the end. A copy of the decision is mailed to the patent owner and any third party with required copies of prior art documents; the signed copy and copies of prior art are made of record in the reexamination electronic file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All correspondence relating to ex parte reexamination should be directed via EFS-Web (registered users), mail to Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam (Central Reexamination Unit), by fax to CRU, or by hand to Customer Service Window. EFS-Web transmissions require certificate of transmission per 37 CFR 1.8(a)(1)(i)(C) and (ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for patent owner and requester to file statements/replies
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director orders reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 304, the patent owner is given a reasonable period, not less than two months from the date a copy of the determination is given or mailed, within which he may file a statement on such question including any amendment and new claims. If the patent owner files such a statement, the requester may file and have considered a reply within two months from date of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision granting the request must set forth the time periods for the patent owner and requester to file their statement and any reply. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted in these proceedings because 1.136 applies only to 'an applicant'; extensions are provided for under 37 CFR 1.550(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner statement content and procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any statement filed by the patent owner shall clearly point out why the subject matter as claimed is not anticipated or rendered obvious by the cited prior art patents or printed publications, either alone or in any reasonable combinations. A copy of the statement must be served by the patent owner on the requester (unless the request was filed by patent owner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided in § 1.510(e), no statement or other response by the patent owner shall be filed prior to the determinations made in accordance with § 1.515 or § 1.520; premature statements will not be acknowledged or considered and will be returned/discarded/expunged. The patent owner's response to an Office action must point out supposed errors and reply to every ground of objection and rejection (37 CFR 1.111(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of prior art submitted after the order
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prior art citations or written statements under 37 CFR 1.501 submitted after the date of the decision on the order are stored until the reexamination is concluded. After conclusion the submission is entered in the patent file. Submissions filed after the date of an order for reexamination will not be considered by the examiner during the reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision denying reexamination — required explanations (22.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner concludes no SNQ has been raised, prepare a decision denying the request using form paragraph 22.02. For each patent and printed publication cited, the decision must indicate why the citation is: (A) cumulative to teachings of earlier concluded examination/review, (B) not available against the claims (e.g., date or not a publication), (C) not important to a reasonable examiner in deciding patentability even though available and not cumulative, or (D) cited in the record and barred by guidelines in MPEP § 2242 II.A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should also respond to substance of each argument raised by requester based on patents or printed publications. If arguments presented are based on non-patent grounds, note improper and do not consider/comment (37 CFR 1.552(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and panel review procedure for decisions (grant or deny)
rubrics_metrics.description: After reexamination file review in the CRU to ensure ready for examination, proceeding is assigned to an examiner who prepares and sets up a panel review conference per MPEP § 2271.01 to discuss issuance of a decision on the request. Examiner may prepare the decision and (where applicable) the first Office action before or after the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preliminary decision to grant or deny is confirmed at conference, decision is completed and signed by examiner with two or more conferees initialing the action. Transmittal form PTOL-465 is used to forward copies of Office actions to third party requester. CRU staff carry out processing (PALM work, scanning) with mailings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition and review procedures for SNQ determinations and denials
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may challenge the correctness of a decision to grant order for ex parte reexamination on basis there is no SNQ by requesting reconsideration of the examiner's SNQ determination (e.g., in a patent owner's statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or response under 37 CFR 1.111). For denials under 35 U.S.C. 302, the requester may seek review by petition to the Director under § 1.181 within one month of mailing of the examiner's determination refusing reexamination (37 CFR 1.515(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ex parte reexamination ordered on or after June 25, 2010, patent owner may seek final agency decision from the Board on SNQ only if patent owner first requested reconsideration before the examiner and then sought Board review; in appeal brief present SNQ issue under separate heading and identify communication first requesting reconsideration. Petitions under 37 CFR 1.181 to vacate an order as 'ultra vires' are rare and will be granted only where USPTO acted in 'brazen defiance' of statutory authorization. Examples of 'appropriate circumstances' to vacate include (A) order not facially based on patents/printed publications, (B) all claims already invalidated by final court decision, (C) reexamination ordered for wrong patent, (D) ordered based on duplicate copy of request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and limits on petitions/oppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 is filed to vacate an order, third party requester may submit an opposition, which must be filed within two weeks of service of the petition to ensure consideration. Filing of a 37 CFR 1.181 petition to vacate is limited to a single submission even if an opposition is filed by a third party requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For petitions under 37 CFR 1.515(c) challenging denials, the CRU Director will review de novo and decision is final and nonappealable. If no timely petition is filed, the determination is final and nonappealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassignment practice after denial-review or when reexamination ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: If petition seeking review of an examiner's denial is granted, the decision should set a two-month period for filing a patent owner's statement and the reexamination file will be returned to the CRU Supervisory Patent Reexamination Specialist (SPRS) for consideration of reassignment. In general, reassignment will be the rule when examiner's determination failed to find any SNQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under normal circumstances, reexamination will not be reassigned to a primary examiner or assistant examiner who was involved in any part of the examination of the patent. Exceptions only in unusual circumstances (e.g., only available examiners have requisite knowledge). If original examiner and denial-examiner are the only examiners with adequate technology knowledge, CRU Director may permit reassignment to original examiner.
